title: One Jar Is Salt  (其中一罐是盐)

segments.t: 周二晚上十点，泰莎上楼休息脚踝后，汉娜和格雷厄姆走进厨房，看到阿瑟正得意地给烘焙台上的两个一模一样的白色陶瓷罐盖上盖子。先完整听一遍吧。
Good night, team! I refilled Tessa's two big white jars so everything looks tidy for dawn!
Wait, Arthur: those two white ceramic jars had little paper labels underneath!
Oh, the paper got damp when I wiped the counter, so I threw both labels away.
Tell me both jars held sugar, boss. Please tell me both were sugar.
No, one bag was fine white caster sugar and one bag was fine white sea salt!
Which jar got the sugar, Arthur: the left jar or the right jar?!
Left! Definitely left... Or did I turn both jars around when I polished the lids?
If Hannah whisks four spoons of sea salt into Wednesday's lemon tarts, the city clerk will run!
Do not panic: tomorrow at six we taste a tiny pinch on a clean spoon before baking!
Write a big red note right now, Hannah! Wait, who is knocking at the front gate at ten at night?!
Look through the lobby window: a woman in a blue coat holding a city folder?!
Wait, is the city clerk not supposed to come Wednesday at three, NOT Tuesday night?!
现在，让我们一句一句来回味这段让人倒吸一口凉气的厨房惨案。
Good night, team! I refilled Tessa's two big white jars so everything looks tidy for dawn!
「晚安，团队！我把泰莎那两个白色大罐子重新装满了，这样天亮时一切看起来都整整齐齐的！」 在这里，前缀 re- 和中文里的“重新”一样，
I refilled
意思是把快空了的罐子重新填满。
Wait, Arthur: those two white ceramic jars had little paper labels underneath!
「等等，阿瑟：那两个白色陶瓷罐子底下可是贴着小纸标签的！」 记住贴在瓶瓶罐罐或者商品上的标签该怎么说：
little paper labels
而 ticket 是用来指车票、门票或收据的。
Oh, the paper got damp when I wiped the counter, so I threw both labels away.
「哦，我擦台面的时候纸弄湿了，所以我就把两张标签都扔了。」 把宾语夹在动词过去式和表示丢弃的副词之间，
threw both labels away
就组成了“扔进垃圾桶”的意思，而 got damp 则是说纸张“变潮湿了”。
Tell me both jars held sugar, boss. Please tell me both were sugar.
「告诉我两个罐子里装的都是糖，老板。求您告诉我两个都是糖。」 用来表示容器里装着或者容纳着什么东西，动词 hold 的过去式
both jars held sugar
在格雷厄姆绝望的祈求中显得十分生动！
No, one bag was fine white caster sugar and one bag was fine white sea salt!
「不，一袋是精细的白幼砂糖，一袋是精细的白海盐！」 在烘焙界非常受欢迎，因为它很容易在奶油里溶解：
caster sugar
指的就是那种颗粒极细的白砂糖，肉眼看过去跟细盐一模一样！
Which jar got the sugar, Arthur: the left jar or the right jar?!
「哪个罐子装了糖，阿瑟：左边的罐子还是右边的罐子？！」 当选择范围局限在眼前的两个具体事物时，我们不用 what 来提问，而是用
Which jar
问到底是哪一个罐子。
Left! Definitely left... Or did I turn both jars around when I polished the lids?
「左边！肯定是左边……还是说我擦亮盖子的时候把两个罐子转了个方向？」 动词词组中间夹着宾语，这个短语
turn both jars around
描绘了他在擦盖子 the lids 时把两个罐子调换了位置或转了个圈。
If Hannah whisks four spoons of sea salt into Wednesday's lemon tarts, the city clerk will run!
「要是汉娜在周三的柠檬挞里拌进去四勺海盐，市政办事员绝对会夺门而出！」 表示把某种配料通过搅拌融入到混合物中，动词和 into 连用：
whisks four spoons of sea salt into
形容从勺子里加进面糊或馅料里的过程。
Do not panic: tomorrow at six we taste a tiny pinch on a clean spoon before baking!
「别慌：明天六点烤之前，我们拿把干净的勺子尝一点点就行了！」 在所有烹饪食谱里都非常实用的词汇，
a tiny pinch
指的就是用两根手指捏起的一点点分量（一撮），而 before baking 则是在介词后面跟上了 -ing 形式。
Write a big red note right now, Hannah! Wait, who is knocking at the front gate at ten at night?!
「现在马上写张大红纸条，汉娜！等等，晚上十点谁在敲前门？！」 又出现了一个 k 和 n 连在一起时不发音的例子，和刚才的 knead 完全一样：
who is knocking
念作 /ˈnɑkɪŋ/，后面用 at 加上敲击的对象（门或窗）。
Look through the lobby window: a woman in a blue coat holding a city folder?!
「从门厅的窗户看出去：一个穿着蓝大衣的女人拿着市政文件夹？！」 表示目光穿过玻璃看出去，英语用介词
Look through the lobby window
而 in a blue coat 则极其简洁地描述了她身上穿着什么样的衣服。
Wait, is the city clerk not supposed to come Wednesday at three, NOT Tuesday night?!
「等等，市政办事员不是应该周三下午三点来吗，而不是周二晚上？！」 在谈论原定计划或约定好的事情时，这个句型绝对少不了：
supposed to come
完完全全对应我们的“按理说”、“本来应该”。听最后一遍这段悬念迭起的场景吧。
Good night, team! I refilled Tessa's two big white jars so everything looks tidy for dawn!
Wait, Arthur: those two white ceramic jars had little paper labels underneath!
Oh, the paper got damp when I wiped the counter, so I threw both labels away.
Tell me both jars held sugar, boss. Please tell me both were sugar.
No, one bag was fine white caster sugar and one bag was fine white sea salt!
Which jar got the sugar, Arthur: the left jar or the right jar?!
Left! Definitely left... Or did I turn both jars around when I polished the lids?

烘焙台上放着没有标签的盐罐和糖罐——周二深夜大门口还传来了带着市政文件的敲门声！第四集到此结束——我们第五集见。
See you tomorrow!
